'''Charles Leonard Bouton''' (April 25, 1869 – February 20, 1922) was an American [[mathematician]].

==Early life and education==
Charles L. Bouton was born in [[St. Louis]], Missouri, where his father was an [[engineer]].<ref name="bull_ams">{{Citation
| last1  = Osgood
| first1 = William F.
| last2  = Coolidge
| first2 = Julian L.
| last3  = Chase
| first3 =George H.
| title   = Charles Leonard Bouton (In Memoriam)
| journal = Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society
| volume  = 28
| issue   = 3
| pages   = 123–124
| year    = 1922
| url     = https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1922-28-03/S0002-9904-1922-03508-2/S0002-9904-1922-03508-2.pdf
| doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1922-03508-2
| doi-access= free
}}</ref> He studied in the public schools of St. Louis. He later received a [[Master of Science]] degree from [[Washington University in St. Louis]].<ref name="bull_ams" /> In 1898 he received his [[doctorate]] from [[Leipzig University]]. His Ph.D. advisor was [[Sophus Lie]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=77959 |title=Charles Leonard Bouton}}</ref>

He married Mary G. Spencer in [[Baltimore]] on June 15, 1907.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-baltimore-sun-grandma-and-grandpa-we/118553723/ |title=Weddings: Bouton-Spencer |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |page=6 |date=1907-06-16 |access-date=2024-08-04 |via=Newspapers.com |archive-date=August 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240804201356/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-baltimore-sun-grandma-and-grandpa-we/118553723/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Teaching==
He taught at the Smith Academy, Washington University and [[Harvard University]].<ref name="bull_ams" /> From 1900 to 1902 Bouton was an editor of the ''[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]''.<ref name="bull_ams" />

He died at his home in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]] on February 20, 1922.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UTY6AQAAMAAJ&pg=PA526 |title=Death of Professor Bouton |magazine=Harvard Alumni Bulletin |volume=XXIV |number=22 |page=526 |date=March 2, 1922 |access-date=2023-05-03 |via=Google Books}}</ref>

==Publications==
In 1902 Bouton published a solution of the game [[Nim]].<ref>{{Citation
| last1  = Bouton
| first1 = C. L.
| title   = Nim, a game with a complete mathematical theory
| journal = Annals of Mathematics
| volume  = 3
| series = 2
| issue  = 1/4
| pages  = 35–39
| year   = 1901–1902
| jstor  = 1967631
| doi=10.2307/1967631
}}</ref>
This result is today viewed as the birth of [[combinatorial game theory]].
